transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-05-14 10:00 UTC | Duration: ~62 minutes | Location: All-hands (Zoom)
Attendees: Alex Ruiz, Maya Patel, Jordan Lee, Priya V., Samir C., plus ~120 remote listeners

Summary: quick leadership lab, short demos, and open floor.

00:00 Alex Ruiz: okay hey everybody um welcome to the bridgekeeper lab uh we're gonna run a tighter format today, 45 minutes of updates then Q&A and two demos, uh please keep questions to chat until the open period.
00:24 Alex Ruiz: quick thanks to hiring and ops for moving the EU region up, that was a big lift.
00:40 Maya Patel: (CTO) quick tech note — the incident signal experiment, so uh we want to surface partial degrade earlier; we're going to route a small percent of traffic to a fallback quantized model and measure customer latency delta and downstream error rates.
01:03 Jordan Lee: (VP Eng) yeah and to add, the goal is not to be perfect it's to be safe-to-fail, um we want clear SLOs; simulated load will run in two waves next week.
01:26 Priya Venkataraman: (Product) top-6 bets — I'm gonna run through these quick: 1) Optimize for 95p latency for streaming, 2) Lower unit cost via smarter batching suggestions, 3) Dedicated pilot for three customers, 4) Private VPC onboarding automation, 5) console UX improvements for rollouts, 6) eval automation for prompt regressions.
02:10 Samir Cole: research — we finished baseline for quantized 4-bit infer and the perf numbers look promising but there's a small hallucination delta in long-form. we'll flag prompts that are sensitive.
02:38 Alex Ruiz: thanks, quick ask: leads, own dashboards for your bet's north star metric and share by Friday.

03:05 (Demo cue — cost dashboard)
03:12 Jordan Lee: demo time, okay sharing screen uh this is the cost dashboard — it's per-route, token split, model variant breakdown. Bear with me if the stream stutters.
03:33 Jordan Lee: you can see token cost by model family; we added a scatter of 95p latency vs unit cost so you can pick the right model for your SLA. note: there's some label issues in the UI — the model name for the redwood-hosted small model shows as 'rw-host-s' in the chart.
04:01 Audience: [chat] "can we export csv?"
04:04 Jordan Lee: yes, export and webhook are coming in next patch.

06:20 Maya Patel: follow-up on infra — we will trial a canary routing policy that prefers cheaper model variants for low-risk customers. privacy note: this will not change data residency.
06:45 Alex Ruiz: ok objections — I already see a thread in the lobby: "does cheaper mean lower quality?" Priya?
06:52 Priya Venkataraman: yeah great question. the plan is to tie quality guardrails to prompt sets; if a prompt fails the eval, it won't be auto-routed. there's an allowlist approach for customers who opt in.
07:22 (small side chatter, someone mutes/unmutes)
07:40 Samir Cole: on evals — we need more labeled prompts from product teams; please add them into the eval bucket; otherwise we risk blind spots.
08:05 Alex Ruiz: hiring cadence — we are opening 12 IC roles in infra and 6 in research this quarter, and we will accelerate contractor-to-FTE conversion for pilots.
08:27 Audience: [chat] "Are we increasing hiring bar for remote?"
08:31 Jordan Lee: hiring bar's consistent; compensation committees are adjusting bands for remote locations.

10:00 (Open Q&A begins)
10:12 Listener 1 (Engineering): Hey quick q — for the Dedicated pilot, what's the expected onboarding time?
10:22 Priya Venkataraman: target is 2 weeks for small customers, 4 weeks for enterprise with network audits; depends on their infra posture.
10:38 Listener 2 (Sales): is pricing set for Reserved capacity?
10:45 Alex Ruiz: not finalized; finance is modeling three tiers and we'll present numbers to SLT next Tuesday.
11:05 Listener 3 (Legal): SSO/SAML and audit logs — how long until the console supports fine-grained RBAC?
11:17 Maya Patel: RBAC is in alpha, audit logs are shipping next month; SSO improvements next quarter.
11:36 (crosstalk, someone says "great work team")

12:10 (Demo 2 — rollout guardrail)
12:15 Priya Venkataraman: demoing an automated rollback policy; um the idea is you can configure a canary percent, lint rules on structured outputs, and auto-rollback on quality regression metrics.
12:40 Priya Venkataraman: note: demo uses synthetic prompts; real customer signals will be more noisy so there is manual override.
13:05 Listener 4 (Ops): can we tune the rollback threshold?
13:09 Priya Venkataraman: yes — threshold and lookback window are editable.

14:04 Alex Ruiz: risk radar quick run: 1) candidate regression on quantized long-form, 2) EU infra capacity during peak, 3) SOC2 remediations backlog, 4) console latency spikes during rollouts.
14:32 Maya Patel: mitigation for 1) is eval gating and smaller canaries; 2) is burst capacity reservation; 3) backlog is being triaged; 4) still investigating root cause, likely a mem leak in the deployment agent.

15:05 (Audience poll)
15:12 Alex Ruiz: poll results — majority want more office hours for release rollouts. we're adding weekly 30m sessions.

15:40 Jordan Lee: operational experiment — doubling tracing retention to 90 days for canaries to get better anomaly detection. we'll measure storage delta and cost.
16:05 Samir Cole: research note — we'll run an A/B for 4-bit vs 8-bit quant on a subset of prompts — request product to nominate sensitive prompt groups.

16:40 (Questions slow down; closing remarks)
16:45 Alex Ruiz: final ask — leads, put owners on the action items, Priya will collect the one-pager. also let's keep slack threads tidy, please.
16:58 Maya Patel: thanks all — for folks in EU timezone we'll post a recap and the recording.
17:12 Priya Venkataraman: recap of next steps in chat.
17:25 Alex Ruiz: meeting adjourned, thanks.

Notes on transcript quality: auto-transcription had a few mislabels on product names (e.g., "rw-host-s" and "quantized 4-bit" occasionally transcribed as "quantize for bit"). There were overlaps and a couple of muted segments not captured.

End of transcript.
